phrases.arabic: مَا قِدِرْتُ أَرُدّ عَلَيْكَ قَبَل شْوَيَّة

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ، مِعَاكَ نُور
dialogue.transliteration: assalamu 3aleekum, mi3aak Noor
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Noor.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلاَمُ، كِيْفَكَ أَنْتَ يَا نُور؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa3aleekum assalam, keefak anta ya Noor?
dialogue.english: Hi Noor, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام الْحَمْد لِلّٰهِ، اتَّصَلْتُ عَلَيْكَ قَبَل شْوَيَّة بَس الْخَطّ كَانَ مَشْغُول
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam il7amdella, attasalt 3aleek 2abel shwayya bas il-khatt kaan mashghool
dialogue.english: All good. I called you a bit ago but the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: إِيْ، كُنْتُ أَتَكَلَّمُ مَعَ أَخِي. آسِف إِنِّي مَا قِدِرْتُ أَرُدّ عَلَيْكَ
dialogue.transliteration: ee, kuntu atkallam ma3a akhi. aasif inni ma 2dirt arudd 3aleek
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry I couldn't answer.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْد لِلّٰهِ عَلَى كُل حَال. أَبْغَى أَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَاكَ عَنْ الْمَوْعِد
dialogue.transliteration: il7amdella 3ala kull 7al. abgha atkallam ma3aak 3an il-maw3id
dialogue.english: It's all good. I want to talk about the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّل، بَس ثَانِيَّة، رَصِيدِي بِيَنْتَهِي
dialogue.transliteration: tafaddal, bas thaniyya, rasiidi biyntahi
dialogue.english: Go ahead, just a second, my credit is about to run out.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: طَيِّب خَلِّينِي أَتَكَلَّمُ بِسُرْعَة قَبْل مَا يَنْقَطِعُ الْخَطّ
dialogue.transliteration: tayyib khallini atkallam bisur3a 2abel ma yingati3 il-khatt
dialogue.english: Okay let me talk fast before the call drops.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: لاَ لاَ، خَلاَص، انْقَطَعَ! تِقْدِرِي تِتَّصِلِي عَلَيَّ بَعِد شْوَيَّة؟
dialogue.transliteration: la la, khalaas, ingata3! tigdari titasili 3alayya ba3d shwayya?
dialogue.english: No no, that's it, it got cut off! Can you call me back?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، حَلْوَ إِنَّك اتَّصَلْتَ أَصْلاً. بَاتَّصِل عَلَيْكَ
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, hallo ennak attasalt aslan. baattasil 3aleek
dialogue.english: Okay, good that you called. I'll call you back.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْد لِلّٰهِ، بَاسْتِنَى
dialogue.transliteration: il7amdella, bastina
dialogue.english: Thank God, I'll wait.

pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: In Hejazi cities, phone calls often open with السلام عليكم and the person answering asks من هذا. Hejazi speakers value warmth, so كيفك comes before the main reason. Ending with الحمد لله or باستني shows respect.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "The line was busy"?
exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.prompt: Your credit ran out. What do you say?
exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase says you have no signal?
exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.prompt: The other person says: "أَلُّو، مِنْ هِذَا؟" Reply.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but too formal for a phone call.

exercises.tip: "mi3aak" is how a caller says "this is".

exercises.prompt: The other person says: "تِقْدِر تِتَّصِل عَلَيَّ بَعِد شْوَيَّة؟" Reply.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but too formal, Hejazis say "baattasil".

exercises.tip: "ba" before a verb means "I will".

exercises.prompt: الْخَطّ كَانَ ___
exercises.tip: Busy line, same word as a busy person.

exercises.prompt: مَا في ___ هِنَا
exercises.tip: Hejazis say shibbaka for the network signal.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The call got cut off on me."
exercises.tip: ma3i means "on me".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Good that you called."
exercises.tip: "hallo" here means good or nice.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: The line was busy.
exercises.tip: Keep the word order as spoken.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: أَلُّو سَامِر، وَيْن نِتْقَابَل بُكْرَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: aaloo Saamer, wayn nitgaabal bukra?
dialogue.english: Hello Samer, where shall we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلاً نُور. خَلِّينَا نِتْقَابَل فِي الْكَافِيه
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan Noor. khallina nitgaabal fil-kaafeeh
dialogue.english: Hi Noor. Let us meet at the cafe.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، سَبْعَة مَاشِي. وَيْن بِالضَّبْط؟
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, sab3a maashi. wayn bid-dabt?
dialogue.english: Fine, seven works. Where exactly?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: الْكَافِيه اللِّي عِنْد الْحَرَم
dialogue.transliteration: il-kaafeeh illi 3ind il-7aram
dialogue.english: The cafe by the Haram.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا عَارْفَة الْمَكَان بِالضَّبْط. بَاقَابِلَك هِنَاك
dialogue.transliteration: ana 3aarfa il-makaan bid-dabt. baagaablak hinaak
dialogue.english: I know exactly where the place is. I will meet you there.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: لَا تِتَأَخَّرِي، أَنَا بَاكُون هِنَاك قَبْلِك
dialogue.transliteration: la titakhkhari, ana baakoon hinaak gablik
dialogue.english: Do not be late, I will be there before you.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: لَوْ تَأَخَّرْت بَاكَلِّمَك
dialogue.transliteration: law ta2akhkhart baakallimak
dialogue.english: If I am late I will call you.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه، نِشُوفِك بُكْرَة
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa2 allah, nishoofik bukra
dialogue.english: God willing, see you tomorrow.

response.english: Do not worry, I will be there before you.

lessons.culture: In Makkah and Jeddah, meetings are often set at a cafe or near a well known landmark like the Haram. Saying إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه after a time is normal and does not mean doubt. Arriving a little late is tolerated, but a quick call to say so is polite.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask "Where should we meet?"
exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase says "Don't be late"?
exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "If you're late, call me"?
exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.prompt: The other person says: "السَّاعَة سَبْعَة تَمَام؟" Reply.
exercises.tip: "maashi" means fine or agreed.

exercises.prompt: The other person says: "وَيْن نِتْقَابَل؟" Reply.
exercises.tip: Reply with just the place.
bid-dabt means exactly.

exercises.prompt: خَلِّينَا نِتْقَابَل فِي ___
exercises.tip: Cafe is borrowed and used as is.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where exactly?"
exercises.tip: wayn is the everyday "where".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll be there before you."
exercises.tip: gabl means before.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I know exactly where the place is.
exercises.tip: Keep the word order as spoken.

phrases.arabic: خَلِّينَا نِلَاقِي يَوْم يِنَاسِبْنَا إِحْنَا الِاثْنَيْن
phrases.transliteration: khallina nilaagi yoom yinaasibna i7na il-ithneen

phrases.arabic: مُمْكِن نِتْقَابَل بَعْد الظُّهْر بَدَل الصُّبْح؟
phrases.transliteration: mumkin nitgaabal ba3d idh-dhuhr badal is-sub7?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: أَلُّو نُور، أَبْغَى أُغَيِّر الْمَوْعِد
dialogue.transliteration: aaloo Noor, abgha ughayyir il-maw3id
dialogue.english: Hello Noor, I want to change the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: خَيْر يَا سَامِر؟
dialogue.transliteration: khayr ya Saamer?
dialogue.english: Is everything alright, Samer?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: صَارَت لِي حَاجَة، مَا أَقْدِر أَجِي الْيَوْم
dialogue.transliteration: saarat li 7aaja, ma agdar aji il-yoom
dialogue.english: Something came up, I can not come today.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: مَا فِي مُشْكِلَة. مُمْكِن نِأَجِّل لِبُكْرَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma fee mushkila. mumkin ni2ajjil li-bukra?
dialogue.english: No problem. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: أَيْوَه، بَس الْمَكَان نَفْسُه وَلَّا تَغَيَّر؟
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, bas il-makaan nafsuh wallaa taghayyar?
dialogue.english: Yes, but is the place still the same?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: نَفْسُه. بَاقَابِلَك يَوْم الْجُمْعَة بَدَل الْخَمِيس
dialogue.transliteration: nafsuh. baagaablak yoom il-jum3a badal il-khamiis
dialogue.english: The same. I will meet you Friday instead of Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، مَاشِي. نِشُوفَك إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, maashi. nishoofak in shaa2 allah
dialogue.english: Fine, agreed. See you, God willing.

lessons.culture: Hejazis usually apologize first and explain briefly, often with just صَارَت لِي حَاجَة, without giving details. Offering a new day in the same breath keeps the friendship warm. Friday is family and prayer time, so check it suits the other person.

exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.tip: Everyday Hejazi, as you would hear it on a call.

exercises.tip: bukra is tomorrow.

phrases.english: Can you pass him a message from me?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: قُل لَهُ يِتَّصِل بِي، وَخَلِّيه يَعْرِف إِنِّي اتَّصَلْت
dialogue.transliteration: gul lahu yittasil bi, wa khallih ya3rif inni ittasalt
dialogue.english: Tell him to call me, and let him know I called.

dialogue.speaker: أخو سامر
dialogue.arabic: بَاقُول لَهُ أَوَّل مَا يِجِي. عِنْدَك رَقَمِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: baagool lahu awwal ma yiji. 3indak ragami?
dialogue.english: I will tell him as soon as he arrives. Do you have my number?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: أَيْوَه، عِنْدِي. مَشْكُور مَرَّة
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, 3indi. mashkoor marra
dialogue.english: Yes, I have it. Thanks a lot.

dialogue.speaker: أخو سامر
dialogue.arabic: الْعَفْو، مَعَ السَّلَامَة
dialogue.transliteration: il-3afw, ma3a s-salaama
dialogue.english: You are welcome, goodbye.

response.english: No, he is not here right now.
I do not know exactly, in a bit.

pair.english: Can you pass him a message from me?

lessons.culture: When the person you want is out, a family member often answers and offers to pass on the message. Asking إِمْتَى بِيِرْجَع and leaving your number is expected, and thanking with مَشْكُور مَرَّة closes the call politely.

challenge.title: Plan a Meeting
challenge.instructions: Imagine you're calling a friend in Hejazi. You want to arrange to meet them, but something has come up for you and you need to change plans.
required_elements: Explanation that something came up (صارت لي حاجة)

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ نُور، كِيْفَك؟
dialogue.transliteration: assalamu 3aleekum Noor, keefik?
dialogue.english: Hello Noor, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ، تَمَام الْحَمْد لِلّٰه
dialogue.transliteration: wa3aleekum assalam, tamaam il7amdella
dialogue.english: Hello, fine, thank God.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: صَارَت لِي حَاجَة، مَا أَقْدِر أَجِي الْيَوْم
dialogue.transliteration: saarat li 7aaja, ma agdar aji il-yoom
dialogue.english: Something came up, I can not come today.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: مَا فِي مُشْكِلَة، مُمْكِن نِأَجِّل لِبُكْرَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma fee mushkila, mumkin ni2ajjil li-bukra?
dialogue.english: No problem, can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: أَيْوَه، بُكْرَة السَّاعَة سَبْعَة فِي الْكَافِيه تَمَام؟
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, bukra is-saa3a sab3a fil-kaafeeh tamaam?
dialogue.english: Yes, tomorrow at seven at the cafe, alright?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام، مَاشِي. مَعَ السَّلَامَة
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, maashi. ma3a s-salaama
dialogue.english: Fine, agreed. Goodbye.
